text:
elaine: Heads up — NimbleThings raised a support ticket: intermittent 429s across dozens of API keys. They said it started after they rolled a new session token strategy yesterday.
michael: What pattern are we seeing? per-key 429s or account-wide? any time-of-day clustering?
kai: Logs show many keys with small bursts ~100-300 rps each but all aligned to ~5s windows. Account-level RPM/TMP looks spiky. Could be token churn causing many short connections.
elaine: PromQL I ran for their customer_id (sanitized): `sum(increase(redwood_requests_total{customer_id="nimblethings"}[1m])) by (api_key)` — hundreds of keys jump simultaneously. Aggregate: ~35k req/min at peak, our per-account cap is 30k/min for their plan.
sam: Interesting — they rotate ephemeral keys per user login, ~180 new keys/min. If those clients warm up concurrently (prefetching, heartbeat), the per-key limits won't help; account-level quotas still hit.
liz: Do we have evidence of proxy or CDN batching those requests into bursts? Any upstream buffering (CF worker, edge LB) that could cause alignment?
ops-bot: trace  -> sample traces show many short-lived sessions doing identical front-end prefetch after key exchange. span ids bunch up at the minute boundaries.
michael: Repro steps we should ask customer for:
• a short HAR or tcpdump from a single client during a spike
• list of key rotation frequency + code snippet of token creation
• confirmation whether they open new HTTP connections per token or reuse pooled connections
kai: Quick mitigation options to propose to customer:
• stop rotating keys per request — consolidate to session-level keys (reuse for N minutes)
• add jitter to key rotation and client prefetches (randomize 0-30s)
• enable client-side exponential backoff + retry-after handling
• if they need many keys, request a quota increase (temp bump) while they rework client behavior
elaine: For our side, eng-runtime suggestions:
• add short-term smoothing at the per-account layer (burst token bucket with leak rate smoothing)
• telemetry flag to surface per-key churn so we can alert earlier
• option to opt-in for request spreading at edge to reduce microbursts
sam: I've drafted message to NimbleThings support ticket with recommended mitigations and an ask for the HAR + snippet. Also suggested temporary quota bump to avoid downtime while they fix.
liz: +1. Also mention client connection pooling — reusing HTTP/2 streams would dramatically lower TPM spikes.
michael: I'll loop in runtime infra (cc @eng-runtime) to discuss a short-term server-side smoothing feature. For now support team: offer a 48h quota increase and the client jitter/backoff checklist.
elaine: Customer-facing FAQ snippet for the ticket (short): "If you rotate API keys very frequently and each new key triggers client warm-up (prefetch/keepalive), you can create short, synchronized bursts that exceed account-level rate limits. Best practice: reuse keys for short-lived sessions, add jitter to rotation schedules, and employ client-side exponential backoff. Contact support for a temporary quota bump while you migrate." :+1:
michael: Good. Anything else?
kai: One more ask — capture a small sample of request headers (x-api-key, connection, user-agent) and a timeline around a spike so we can correlate key churn to bursts.
elaine: Perfect. I'll send the template and request those items now. Closing thread once we confirm quota bump and they provide HAR. :eyes:
